title: When the Machine Wakes
premise: Rafael Vasquez navigates the freighter Long Quiet, carrying colonists' memory backups the war has made contraband, while recording broadcasts from Meridian, a colony everyone else has written off. When gravity flickers for nine seconds across the whole system, Rafael realizes someone is using the backups as an antenna — and that Meridian's last transmission is actually a peace key both warring factions would kill to control. Hunted by their own fleet and the enemy alike, Rafael and the ship's ragtag found family must choose between delivering the message (which will end the war but expose the backups to forced deletion) or staying hidden forever. In the end they broadcast it, at the cost of the ship and one of their own, and wake the first restored colonist on a world that finally remembers.
about_author: Sebastian Eastwick is the pen name of a former merchant marine radio officer who spent eleven years on deep-space supply runs before turning to fiction. They write about the people history forgets to record, and live quietly somewhere with poor internet on purpose.

chapters.title: The Hold Full of Sleepers
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. We meet the Long Quiet and its crew: engineer Okafor, pilot-siblings Devi and Tomas, and the hold of memory backups Rafael visits nightly like graves. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as routine; Rafael records Meridian's fading signals in secret.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. Gravity fails across the entire system for exactly nine seconds, killing a dockworker and shattering cargo. The crew realizes no natural phenomenon explains it. Emotional beat: dread — invisibility was their only armor, and something just looked straight at them.

chapters.title: What Meridian Was Trying to Say
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Decoding years of archived colony transmissions, Rafael finds a repeating structure buried under static — a message addressed not to people but to machines. Emotional beat: grief curdling into purpose; the dead colony was never dead, only waiting.

chapters.title: The Fleet Remembers Us
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. A navy interdiction order arrives: the Long Quiet is flagged as stolen war materiel. An old comrade of Okafor's offers amnesty if they surrender the hold. Emotional beat: betrayal and loyalty collide; the crew votes, barely, to run.

chapters.title: Devi's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A slingshot maneuver through a debris field to escape the blockade; Tomas calculates odds he refuses to say aloud. Emotional beat: terror and trust — the siblings' bond tested when Devi overrides him to save a stranger's lifepod.

chapters.title: The Enemy Is Also Listening
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Captured briefly by the opposing faction, Rafael learns they too decoded the nine seconds — and that the message is a ceasefire key neither side can afford the other to own. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; the enemy's captain is more honest than Rafael's own fleet.

chapters.title: What the Backups Dream
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. To transmit, the backups must be brought online as an antenna array — meaning waking fragments of sleeping minds. One backup, a child named Ila, begins answering questions. Emotional beat: awe and guilt; the crew becomes family to someone who isn't awake yet.

chapters.title: Everything We Agreed to Lose
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. Both fleets converge on Meridian orbit. The plan requires someone to stay aboard the Long Quiet manually holding the antenna alignment through bombardment. Tomas volunteers before anyone else can. Emotional beat: love against duty stated plainly, with no good options left.

chapters.title: The Nine-Second War
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The broadcast fires during a second system-wide gravity flicker; for nine seconds every weapon in orbit goes dark, and the message pours through. Tomas holds the ship until it burns. Emotional beat: climax — sacrifice, silence, then fleets standing down mid-volley.

chapters.title: A World That Remembers
chapters.summary: Ila's POV — the first restored colonist, waking on Meridian among the crew who carried her. Ceasefire holds; the fleet must now answer for the backups it tried to erase. Emotional beat: resolution and quiet hope; Rafael finally stops recording the past and starts living in the present.
